description:
CSUTLDTC, the called date-validation subprogram, exercised as the @Service it became (util.DateUtilityJob) and never through a JobLauncher or an HTTP layer: no EXEC PGM= anywhere in app/jcl or app/proc names it, and it is CALLed four times from two online programs - CORPT00C at L392 and L412, COTRN02C at L393 and L413. LS-DATE='2022XYZ19 ' and LS-DATE-FORMAT='YYYYMMMDD ' are this case's two LINKAGE SECTION parameters (L84-L85), each written out to the declared PIC X(10) width so the trailing space of each is visible rather than left to a pad; LS-RESULT PIC X(80) (L86) is the entire output and is asserted below as the single WS_MESSAGE_80 line. The program declares no SELECT, opens no file and issues no EXEC CICS, so it seeds no dataset, writes no record, paints no screen and takes no job parameter; its whole observable behaviour is the 80 bytes L97 moves into LS-RESULT and the severity L98 moves into RETURN-CODE. This case pins arm 6 of the EVALUATE TRUE at L128-L149: FC-INVALID-MONTH, whose 88-level VALUE is X'000309D559C3C5C5' (L67). Severity and message number are DECODED from those bytes rather than interpolated - CASE-1-CONDITION-ID (L71-L73) declares SEVERITY PIC S9(4) BINARY then MSG-NO PIC S9(4) BINARY, so the leading halfword 0x0003 is the severity and the second halfword 0x09D5 is 9*256+213 = 2517, while the trailing 59 C3 C5 C5 is the severity-control byte and the facility identifier 'CEE' in EBCDIC and takes no part in the message. The numeric REDEFINES views WS-SEVERITY-N (L44) and WS-MSG-NO-N (L47) written at L123 and L124 therefore render '0003' and '2517' zero-filled to four digits, RETURN-CODE is 3, and the arm moves 'Invalid month  ' into WS-RESULT PIC X(15) (L140) - a literal the author already padded to fifteen, so the two trailing spaces are inside the quotes in the source and are reproduced verbatim here rather than being a pad this fixture applied. What makes this case distinct from its two siblings on the same arm is the ROUTE, not the arm: case12 ('2022-00-15') and case13 ('2022-13-15') both present a correctly shaped numeric MM and fail the range check for 1 to 12, whereas this case's mask asks for MMM - the three-character month ABBREVIATION field - and 'XYZ' is not one of the twelve names, so it is refused at the name lookup, strictly before the numeric range test the other two reach. Three cases, one arm, three genuinely different paths, which is exactly the collapse a field-for-field diff must be able to see. It is equally distinct from case15 ('QQQQ-MM-DD'), where the MASK itself cannot be parsed and the outcome is FC-BAD-PIC-STRING 2518 (L68, L141-L142): here the mask parses perfectly - greedily as YYYY, then MMM before the shorter MM, then DD, then the trailing space as a literal delimiter, consuming 4+3+2+1 = 10 input characters - and it is the DATE that fails. It is distinct again from case18 ('ABCD-EF-GH'), which is FC-NON-NUMERIC-DATA 2520: that case puts letters where DIGITS were declared, while this one puts letters where letters were declared and merely gets the wrong three. Neither in-repository caller passes this mask - both declare WS-DATE-FORMAT PIC X(10) VALUE 'YYYY-MM-DD' (CORPT00C L72, COTRN02C L60) - so this case exercises the subprogram's own published byte contract beyond the single mask its callers happen to use, which is the contract a CALLed subprogram is obliged to honour. Both callers would reject this result: each accepts severity '0000' and additionally tolerates only message number '2513' (CORPT00C L396-L399, COTRN02C L397-L400), so severity 0003 with 2517 drives 'Start Date - Not a valid date...', 'End Date - Not a valid date...', 'Orig Date - Not a valid date...' and 'Proc Date - Not a valid date...' at the four CALL sites. The two X(10) spans of the message behave ASYMMETRICALLY and that asymmetry is the point of this file. WS-DATE at offset 45 is deliberately NOT the date as supplied: L105-L106 moves LENGTH OF LS-DATE - the DECLARED length, hence always 10 - into VSTRING-LENGTH, L107-L108 puts the date into both VSTRING-TEXT and WS-DATE, and L122 then moves the whole WS-DATE-TO-TEST group into WS-DATE PIC X(10), overwriting L107; because that group opens with Vstring-length PIC S9(4) BINARY (L26) the receiver takes the leftmost ten bytes, so the two-byte binary halfword X'000A' survives and only the first eight text bytes '2022XYZ1' follow it, the trailing '9' and its space truncated on the right. WS-DATE-FMT at offset 66 is by contrast CLEAN: L111-L113 set it by an ordinary X(10) to X(10) move BEFORE the CALL and L122 targets WS-DATE alone, so the mask is echoed back verbatim including its own trailing space - no two-byte prefix, no blanking, and no correction of a mask the program rejected. Both behaviours are preserved as observed rather than tidied. The 80-byte geometry is mechanical: the thirteen storage spans declared at L42-L57 sum to 4+11+4+1+15+1+9+10+1+10+10+1+3 = 80, the two numeric REDEFINES overlays contribute none, and INITIALIZE WS-MESSAGE at L90 does not clear FILLER, so the three literals 'Mesg Code:' in an X(11) span (one trailing space), 'TstDate:' in an X(09) span (one trailing space) and 'Mask used:' in an X(10) span (no padding at all) always appear. Both callers corroborate those offsets independently of WS-MESSAGE by redefining the returned 80 bytes as CSUTLDTC-RESULT-SEV-CD X(04) + FILLER X(11) + CSUTLDTC-RESULT-MSG-NUM X(04) + CSUTLDTC-RESULT-MSG X(61) (CORPT00C L132-L136, COTRN02C L65-L69), which is where the severity at [0,4) and the message number at [15,19) are read from in production. Expected values are STATICALLY DERIVED by structured reading of app/cbl/CSUTLDTC.cbl - the 01 WS-MESSAGE declaration at L42-L57 summed span by span, the nine feedback tokens at L62-L70, the group move at L122 and the EVALUATE at L128-L149 - and were NOT captured from, recorded against or replayed from any execution of the COBOL, which is impossible in this environment: PROCEDURE DIVISION USING at L88 makes this a subprogram the available compiler refuses to build as an executable, and no Language Environment services are reachable, so the CALL "CEEDAYS" at L116 that decides every outcome has no implementation to call and is reproduced by a hand-written total guard chain. Only the provenance of the expectation is substituted; the twenty-case set, the field-by-field diff and the diff-count-of-zero gate all stand.

THE TWO CALL PARAMETERS, DECLARED RATHER THAN SELECTED IN JAVA. unitStimulus.linkage carries this case's whole input: LS-DATE = '2022XYZ19 ' and LS-DATE-FORMAT = 'YYYYMMMDD ', each written out to the ten characters PIC X(10) declares at app/cbl/CSUTLDTC.cbl:84-85 with every trailing space visible - a mask longer than ten characters is TRUNCATED by the receiving field, and the truncation changes the message number, so the width has to be readable at the point the value is written. CSUTLDTC seeds no dataset and drives no screen, so these two values are the only thing a case varies; they used to live in a table in CSUTLDTCParityTest keyed by 'case01'..'case20', which meant this file stated an eighty-byte result with nothing in it to say what was validated, and cases that differ only in their input were indistinguishable on disk.
